title: Parseval EEGNet: Enhancing Robustness of EEG-Based BCIs Against Adversarial Attacks
summary: We propose Parseval EEGNet, a modified EEGNet architecture with Parseval tight frame constraints on convolutional layers to improve robustness against adversarial perturbations in EEG-based BCIs. By ensuring Lipschitz continuity, the model maintains stable predictions under input variations while preserving classification accuracy. We validate the approach on public EEG datasets with adversarial attacks, comparing performance against standard EEGNet and Parseval networks from computer vision.
gap: While EEGNet generalizes well across BCI paradigms, existing EEG-based CNN models lack robustness guarantees against adversarial examples, a critical concern for safety-critical BCI applications. Prior robustness methods (e.g., Parseval networks) are unexplored in EEG domains.
approach: Integrate Parseval tight frame constraints into EEGNet's convolutional layers via spectral normalization during training. This maintains weight matrices as approximately orthogonal, bounding Lipschitz constants to improve robustness without sacrificing accuracy.
evaluation: Compare Parseval EEGNet with baseline EEGNet and Parseval networks on datasets from [ref-001] using FGSM/PGD attacks. Metrics include clean/test accuracy, robustness score (CLEVER from [ref-009]), and adversarial loss. Cross-subject generalization is tested via leave-one-subject-out validation.

title: MOABB-Integrated Adversarial Training for Generalizable Robust EEG Decoders
summary: We develop an adversarial training framework integrated with the MOABB benchmarking platform to improve generalization of EEG classifiers against unseen attacks. By exposing models to diverse adversarial examples during training across multiple datasets, we enhance robustness without sacrificing cross-paradigm performance. Validation uses MOABB's standardized pipelines and novel attack transferability metrics.
gap: Current BCI robustness evaluations focus on single datasets or attacks, failing to assess generalization. MOABB enables multi-dataset benchmarking but lacks adversarial robustness analysis, leaving a gap in scalable, reproducible robustness validation.
approach: Extend MOABB with adversarial training modules, incorporating PGD and CW attacks during training. Train EEGNet variants on aggregated datasets from [ref-007], applying dynamic attack schedules to simulate real-world threat diversity.
evaluation: Benchmark trained models on MOABB's 12 datasets using attack transferability matrices. Metrics include accuracy under white-box/black-box attacks, CLEVER scores, and comparison with non-adversarially trained baselines. Cross-paradigm robustness is assessed via paradigm-shuffled splits.

title: Safety-Certified EEGNet via Semidefinite Programming for Implantable BCIs
summary: We present a safety-certified EEGNet variant using semidefinite programming (SDP) to provide formal robustness guarantees for implantable BCIs. By bounding output variations under input perturbations, the model ensures reliable operation in safety-critical scenarios. Validation includes SDP-based verification and physical adversarial testing on motor imagery datasets.
gap: Implantable BCIs require provable safety guarantees, but existing EEG models lack formal robustness certification. SDP methods from [ref-005] and [ref-020] are untested in EEG domains, leaving a gap in certified robust BCI design.
approach: Apply SDP-based quadratic constraint programming to EEGNet, modeling activation functions as convex potentials. Derive layer-wise Lipschitz bounds via SDP relaxation, ensuring output stability under bounded input perturbations during inference.
evaluation: Compare certified robustness bounds with empirical attack success rates on motor imagery datasets. Metrics include verified perturbation radii, CLEVER scores, and comparison with Parseval EEGNet. Physical adversarial testing uses noise-injected EEG signals from [ref-006].
